newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Thousands in Brussels march over child sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Thousands in Brussels march over child sex scandal.

text.p: A march by an estimated 275,000 Belgians and sympathisers from neighbouring countries, one of the largest in the country's history, began at 2:30 p.m. (1230 GMT) on Sunday in Brussels, police sources said.

The beginning of the demonstration -- an outpouring of anger and frustration aimed at the political and judicial classes in the wake of a kidnap, murder and child sex scandal -- was held up for half an hour due to congestion at the starting point.

Under leaden skies, people from all ages and walks of life, carrying white balloons and flowers and some wearing white clothes and caps as symbol of hope, peacefully protested against a legal system that failed to stop a deadly paedophile ring.
"So far everything is very calm," a police spokesman said, noting that many of the marchers were parents and children.

Thousands were still arriving at the capital's North Station -- the rallying point -- on packed trains, police said. Trains from all over the country were being stopped just outside Brussels to avoid overcrowding at stations.
The marchers heeded calls for calm from King Albert, Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene and the parents of missing children and the victims, the organisers of the "White March."
But 1,400 police officers were on hand even so.

One marcher, Gerda Zammattio from the town of Mechelen with three-year-old Naomi, said, "I am here to show solidarity with the parents. What has happened in the last few weeks moved me greatly. The system must become more humane."
One Dutch-language banner read, "Ashamed to be Belgian."
Flemish protestors wore stickers across their foreheads saying, "Stop the cover-up."

The march, not only aimed at what is seen as an incompetent law and order system, but also to show general dissatisfaction with the political class, is part of a groundswell of public emotion that one government minister said must be heeded.
At the heart of the rally is a national need to express sympathy with the victims of a gang alleged to have been led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.
Four young girls died in the hands of the gang -- two were starved to death. Two others were rescued, but not before they were sexually abused.

Dutroux, one of 13 people so far charged in connection with the case, was released 10 years early in 1992 from a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape. Scores of videos with child porn were seized.
The White March is the culmination of a week of protests which broke out spontaneously after Belgium's top court removed a popular magistrate from investigations into the ring.

The Cour de Cassation ruled that magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte had compromised himself by accepting a free dinner from the Marc et Corine group that specialises in helping the parents of missing children.

The ruling, following the letter rather than the spirit of the law, prompted an already morally-outraged public to take to the streets amid widespread allegations of a looming high-level cover-up and call for a radical clean-up of the justice system.
The march was planned before Comnerotte's dismissal, but gained momentum since.
Workers at national airline Sabena, carrying white armbands, stopped work for five minutes on Sunday morning in support of the march and were due to do so again in the afternoon.
